handbook_metadata.title: Nuclear Medicine Terminology Handbook
handbook_metadata.description: Domain vocabulary pack for training and structuring a Radiology & Nuclear Medicine Voice Dictation Assistant.
handbook_metadata.safety_boundary: This is a terminology and language resource, not a clinical protocol or a substitute for a qualified nuclear medicine physician. The assistant must preserve what the clinician dictated, flag uncertainty, and never invent findings, diagnoses, administered activities, or treatment instructions.

pet_ct.definition: Positron emission tomography; functional imaging based on detection of paired photons produced after positron annihilation.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Functional imaging method; never substitute with SPECT or CT.

pet_ct.definition: Computed tomography; cross-sectional anatomical imaging.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Anatomical imaging; preserve dictated modality.

pet_ct.definition: Combined PET and CT examination providing functional and anatomical information.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Combined functional and anatomical examination.

pet_ct.definition: Fluorodeoxyglucose, commonly 18F-FDG; a glucose analogue used in many oncologic, inflammatory and other PET studies.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Glucose analogue tracer.

pet_ct.definition: Fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose; pronounce and transcribe isotope and tracer name carefully.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Preserve isotope and tracer name carefully. Never confuse with I-131.

pet_ct.definition: Gallium-68-labelled PSMA radiopharmaceutical family; do not assume a specific compound if not dictated.

pet_ct.definition: Tracer excretion through the urinary tract; commonly relevant to renal/bladder activity for certain tracers.

pet_ct.definition: Reference uptake in the liver, often used in qualitative PET assessment when appropriate.

pet_ct.safe_usage: Reference comparator for visual Deauville scoring and PERCIST.

pet_ct.definition: A five-point visual scale used in specific lymphoma response-assessment settings; use only when appropriate and reported.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Use only 1 to 5 visual scale for lymphoma response assessment when dictated.

pet_ct.safe_usage: Standardized criteria for metabolic response; do not confuse with RECIST.

pet_ct.definition: A response-assessment category used in applicable criteria; should not be assigned automatically without required data and physician review.

pet_ct.definition: Volume of tumour tissue defined using a specified PET segmentation method.

pet_ct.definition: A semi-quantitative measure combining metabolic tumour volume and mean uptake in FDG PET.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Product of MTV and SUVmean.

pet_ct.definition: A lymphatic structure; document anatomical station, size and tracer uptake where available.

pet_ct.safe_usage: Origin lesion of malignancy as established clinically.

pet_ct.definition: A lesion interpreted as secondary spread; the assistant must not infer this from uptake alone.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Must not infer metastasis from uptake alone without clinical context.

pet_ct.definition: Uptake that appears suspicious but is not due to the disease being investigated.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Tracer concentration caused by inflammation, infection, or healing.

pet_ct.definition: A study that does not demonstrate disease that is actually present; detectability depends on tracer and other factors.
pet_ct.safe_usage: Underlying disease undetected due to size, motion, or low tracer avidity.

gamma_camera_spect.definition: A radiopharmaceutical used in selected myocardial perfusion, parathyroid and other imaging protocols.
gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Myocardial perfusion and parathyroid adenoma localization.

gamma_camera_spect.definition: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy using an appropriate iminodiacetic acid radiopharmaceutical.
gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Hepatobiliary clearance, acute cholecystitis, and biliary leak evaluation.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Acquired post-exercise or pharmacological vasodilator/inotropic stress.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Baseline myocardial perfusion status.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Simultaneous evaluation of regional wall motion and ejection fraction.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Preserve explicit percentage (e.g. 58%) and acquisition technique.

gamma_camera_spect.definition: Dynamic renal scintigraphy used to assess renal perfusion, function and drainage.
gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Time-activity curves for renal vascular transit, uptake, and clearance.

gamma_camera_spect.definition: Nuclear medicine assessment of gastric emptying using a defined meal and protocol.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Subsegmental, segmental, or non-segmental perfusion deficit.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Matched vs mismatched with perfusion defect.

gamma_camera_spect.safe_usage: Dose infiltration at venous injection site; document dose infiltration impact.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Treatment using a radiopharmaceutical that delivers radiation to targeted tissues.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Therapeutic administration delivering internal ionizing radiation.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: An approach pairing molecular imaging with a related targeted radionuclide therapy where clinically appropriate.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Pairing molecular diagnostic imaging with targeted therapeutic radionuclides.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Iodine-131, used in selected thyroid-related diagnostic or therapeutic contexts depending on protocol.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Preserve isotope strictly. Never confuse with F-18.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Therapy using radioactive iodine for selected thyroid conditions under specialist care.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Thyroid cancer ablation or hyperthyroidism therapy.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Lutetium-177, a therapeutic radionuclide used in selected targeted therapies.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Beta-emitting therapeutic radionuclide. Never auto-correct to Ga-68.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Lutetium-177-labelled DOTATATE used for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy in appropriate patients.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy agent.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy; targeted treatment for selected somatostatin-receptor-positive disease.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Targeted treatment for neuroendocrine tumours.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Lutetium-177-labelled PSMA-targeted therapy for selected prostate cancer patients.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Targeted prostate cancer beta-emitter therapy.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Yttrium-90, a therapeutic radionuclide used in selected treatments, including certain radioembolization procedures.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Pure beta-emitter used in radioembolization and radiosynovectomy.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Delivery of radioactive microspheres into selected arterial territories, commonly in liver-directed treatment.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Transarterial radioembolization (TARE/SIRT).

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Radium-223, a therapeutic alpha-emitting radionuclide used in a specific clinical setting.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Bone-targeted alpha-emitting therapy for metastatic CRPC.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Strontium-89, a radionuclide historically used for palliation of selected painful bone metastases; current use depends on local practice.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Bone pain palliation beta-emitter.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Samarium-153, a radionuclide used in selected bone-pain palliation settings.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Bone pain palliation complex (Sm-153 EDTMP).

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: A radionuclide that emits alpha particles; examples in therapy include Ac-225 and Ra-223.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: High linear energy transfer (LET) radionuclide.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: A radionuclide that emits beta particles; examples used in therapy include Lu-177 and Y-90.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Intermediate range therapeutic emission.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Emission of gamma photons; may be relevant to imaging or radiation characteristics of a radionuclide.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Allows post-therapy imaging and external radiation assessment.

therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Amount of activity administered (MBq/GBq/mCi); never confuse with absorbed dose (Gy).

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Energy deposited per unit mass, measured in gray (Gy).
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Energy deposited per mass unit; measured in Gray (Gy).

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Radioactive decay rate, commonly expressed in becquerels (Bq), MBq or GBq.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Physical decay rate measured in Bq, MBq, GBq, or mCi.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Time required for radioactive activity to decrease by half; distinguish physical, biological and effective half-life.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Distinguish physical half-life from biological and effective clearance half-life.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Patient-specific safety instructions provided by the treating nuclear medicine team.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Contact distance, hydration, and hygiene protocols.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: A planned treatment administration within a course; document cycle number only when stated.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Document cycle number (e.g. cycle 1, cycle 2) only when explicitly dictated.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Imaging acquired after therapeutic radiopharmaceutical administration.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Acquired at 24h, 48h, or 72h post administration.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Clinical, biochemical or imaging change assessed using the relevant follow-up approach.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Biochemical (e.g. PSA, chromogranin A) or imaging evaluation.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Potential adverse effect relevant to certain targeted radionuclide therapies; clinical assessment belongs to the treating team.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Dose-limiting risk for PSMA therapies; clinical assessment belongs to physician.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Dry mouth; may be relevant in selected therapeutic contexts.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Symptom of salivary hypofunction following PSMA or I-131 therapies.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Kidney toxicity; risk and monitoring depend on the specific therapy and patient.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Renal risk factor; requires amino acid co-infusion monitoring.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Reduced bone-marrow activity, potentially affecting blood cell counts.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Hematologic monitoring for anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Estimation or measurement of radiation absorbed dose to tissues or organs.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Quantitative absorbed dose estimation (Gy/GBq).

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Documented informed-consent process handled by the responsible clinical team.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Formal clinical documentation; assistant must not generate or bypass consent.

therapeutic_theranostics.definition: Applicable radiation-safety criteria for patient discharge or release, determined by local regulations and the responsible service.
therapeutic_theranostics.safe_usage: Local radiation regulatory criteria for patient discharge.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Different radionuclides (Diagnostic PET vs Therapeutic/Diagnostic Thyroid)
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Preserve the isotope exactly and flag uncertainty. Never auto-convert one to the other.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Diagnostic vs Therapeutic roles (Gallium-68 diagnostic vs Lutetium-177 therapy)
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different radionuclides with commonly different diagnostic/therapeutic roles; never auto-correct one to the other.
Distinct tracer names; do not normalize as synonyms.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Different molecular targets (Prostate-specific membrane antigen vs Somatostatin receptor)
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different molecular targets; retain exactly what was dictated.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Different imaging acquisition methods and physics
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different imaging methods; never substitute one for the other.
Different modalities; preserve the dictated modality.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Critical laterality reversal in paired organs or lymph nodes
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Critical laterality error; require explicit confirmation if audio is unclear. Never silently choose left or right.
Negation changes meaning; do not infer or silently repair.

high_risk_confusables.pair: No evidence of vs evidence of
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Negation phrase must be preserved exactly.
Opposite meaning; flag unclear comparative words.
Degree terms should not be changed by language-model rewriting.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Magnitude error of 1000x in administered radioactivity
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Units differ by a factor of 1,000; never infer or convert without explicit source and validation.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Voxel peak uptake vs mean region-of-interest uptake
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different metrics; preserve the reported metric.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Misclassifying treatment administration as an imaging scan
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different clinical purposes; do not classify from tracer name alone.
Different quantities and units; never treat as interchangeable.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Lymphatic station vs pulmonary parenchymal nodule
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Different anatomical structures; verify when speech is unclear.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Truncated decimal places or altered metric units
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Keep units and decimal places; ask for confirmation if uncertain.

high_risk_confusables.danger_type: Hallucinating prior dates or cycle sequences
high_risk_confusables.safe_usage_guidance: Do not infer dates or cycle numbers from context without explicit confirmation.

core_and_reporting_language.definition: Medical specialty using radiopharmaceuticals to assess physiology, diagnose disease, and in selected cases deliver targeted therapy.
A medicinal product containing a radionuclide, used for imaging or therapy.
An unstable nuclide that emits radiation; examples include F-18, Ga-68, Tc-99m, I-123, I-131 and Lu-177.
A radiopharmaceutical used to trace a biological process or distribution.
Accumulation of a tracer in a tissue or structure; its significance depends on tracer, physiology and context.
Expected tracer activity in normal tissues for that specific radiopharmaceutical.
Uptake outside an expected pattern; not automatically proof of malignancy.
How a radiopharmaceutical distributes through the body.
Degree to which a lesion or tissue demonstrates uptake of a particular tracer.

core_and_reporting_language.term: Hot spot / focus of increased uptake
core_and_reporting_language.definition: An area with relatively higher tracer activity; describe location and context rather than assigning a diagnosis automatically.
An area with relatively reduced or absent tracer activity.
A non-pathological variation in tracer distribution or anatomy.
Reduction in detected photon intensity as radiation passes through tissue.
Correction method used to compensate for photon attenuation, commonly using CT information in PET/CT and SPECT/CT.
Underestimation or distortion of activity in small structures due to limited spatial resolution.
Standardized uptake value; a semi-quantitative PET measure whose interpretation depends on acquisition and patient factors.
Maximum voxel SUV within a defined region of interest.
Mean SUV within a defined region of interest.
A selected image region used for measurement or analysis.
A display that projects the highest voxel value along each viewing ray.
Alignment or combined display of functional and anatomical images.
An observation unrelated to the primary clinical question that may require appropriate review.
Comparison with another modality, such as diagnostic CT, MRI or ultrasound.
Limited to a localized area.
Distributed broadly through a tissue or organ.
Non-uniform in appearance or tracer distribution.
Uniform in appearance or tracer distribution.
Similar on both sides / differing between sides.
Expected distribution of a particular tracer under the relevant conditions.
Relatively increased activity; requires context and should not automatically be equated with malignancy.
Relatively decreased activity.
A reporting phrase that should only be used when supported by the actual interpreted study.
Interpret in the context of symptoms, examination and other clinical information.
Compare with CT, MRI or another relevant modality.
Not confidently classifiable based on the available information.
A finding that does not uniquely indicate a particular cause.
Increase compared with a suitable prior examination.
Decrease compared with a suitable prior examination.
No meaningful change identified using the applicable comparison.
A finding not present or not reported on the relevant prior study; comparison must be reliable.
Prior examination used for comparison.
A factor that limits image quality or interpretation.
Image interpretation affected by patient or organ motion.
State when no suitable comparison examination is available.
Right, left or bilateral; a critical field that must not be guessed.
Direction from head toward feet; often used for lesion extent.
Common anatomical image planes.
Abnormal enlargement or involvement of lymph nodes; diagnosis depends on context.
Relating to bone.
Relating to internal organs.
Outside bone.
Within the skull.
Relating to the mediastinum.
Located behind the peritoneal cavity.
Relating to the liver.
Relating to the spleen.
Relating to the adrenal gland.
Relating to the kidney.
Relating to the pelvis.

abbreviations_and_units.usage_note: Context may have other meanings, expand on first use.
Confirm context because abbreviations can be ambiguous.
Unit of radioactive activity (10^9 Bq). 1 GBq = 1,000 MBq.
